column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/python-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name>
# WHAT THIS PINS
#   Two jobs, one edge: bump -> ship. `bump` is gated only on the actor (bot
#   loop-break); `ship` is gated only on `needs.bump.outputs.bumped == 'true'`
#   and inherits skip-when-my-dependency-skipped (no always() anywhere here).
#   So the whole selection surface is (actor x bumped), and every row below is
#   one cell of it. Rows 1-4 also carry the privacy axis - see the next block
#   for why, because that is the point of the sweep.
# THE PRIVACY AXIS IS DECLARED AND DELIBERATELY INERT - READ THIS BEFORE
# DELETING A ROW AS A DUPLICATE.
#   The sweep exists because cargo-auto-release's publish jobs carry
#   `&& !github.event.repository.private`, so a private repo bumps, tags,
#   pushes and publishes NOTHING while reporting success. THIS WORKFLOW HAS NO
#   SUCH GUARD. `github.event.repository.private` appears twice in this file
#   (lines 53 and 85) and BOTH are inside `runs-on:` - runner routing, not job
#   selection. Neither `if:` mentions it, and the caller that dispatches here
#   (auto-release.yml's `python` job, gated only on repo-type) does not gate on
#   it either.
#   Consequence, asserted by rows public-bump and private-bump-publishes-anyway
#   being IDENTICAL in expectation: python-auto-release publishes to pypi.org
#   from a PRIVATE repo. That is the opposite of the cargo family's posture. It
#   is pinned here as measured behaviour, NOT endorsed - if the fleet posture is
#   'never publish from a private repo', the fix belongs in the workflow and
#   private-bump-publishes-anyway then flips to expect-skip=ship in the same PR.
#   The two rows are kept as a PAIR on purpose: one row alone cannot show that
#   the privacy value changes nothing, and 'changes nothing' is the finding.
#   The key is declared in every case even though no condition reads it, so the
#   day a guard is added the table already carries the axis it must be asserted
#   on, and the rows differ by the value that will then matter.
# NO STATUS FUNCTIONS ARE SUPPLIED because no condition calls one. always() is
# absent from this workflow, which is exactly why `ship` cannot pick a run up
# after `bump` skips - see bot-actor-no-loop.
# 1. The happy path. A public repo bumped, so it must also ship.
public-bump
# 2. THE SWEEP ROW. Same input, private repo. `ship` STILL RUNS - unguarded.
#    Flip this to expect-skip=ship only together with a workflow change.
private-bump-publishes-anyway
# 3. Nothing to release: bump ran and reported no version change, so ship is
#    skipped by its own condition (not by needs-propagation).
public-no-bump
# 4. The private half of row 3, proving privacy is inert in the no-bump cell
#    too - so a future guard cannot be mistaken for this row already covering it.
private-no-bump
# 5. Loop-break: the bot's own push must not re-trigger a release. `bump` is
#    skipped by actor, and `ship` is skipped by needs-propagation - the empty
#    `bumped` value models a SKIPPED upstream, which is distinct from 'false'.
#    Nothing runs; the run is green and empty, by design.
bot-actor-no-loop
